      intelligence, just as child is killed by an enraged snake. That man has no

      perplexity when an occasion for the exercise of vigour presents itself.

      can secure exemption from (spiritual) misery; and the means of salvation
      found, he must then free himself from sensuality. The man who has attained
      a high state of spiritual knowledge is always conscious of the great
      deficiency (instability) of all matter. Such a person keeping in view the

      in the practice of virtue.’

      me to recite,—the virtue of women’s devotion to their husbands and

      discourse.’”
